title: Polynomial structure and behavior
purpose: Use algebraic structure to explain a polynomial's graph and recover its zeros.

lessons.title: Degree and end behavior
lessons.objective: Predict a polynomial's end behavior and possible number of turning points from its leading term.
lessons.coverage: Polynomial versus nonpolynomial rules, degree, leading coefficient, even/odd powers, and upper bounds on turning points without claiming that every bound is attained.
lessons.activity: Compare a polynomial with its leading term at expanding viewing scales and explain why local shape can differ while far-end behavior agrees.
families: Classify end behavior from symbolic rules
Match a graph description to possible degrees and leading-coefficient signs
lessons.generatorRules: Never allow the leading coefficient to vanish; distinguish an upper bound from an exact turning-point count. Include odd and even degree with each sign.
lessons.commonError: Using the constant term to predict the ends or treating degree minus one as an exact turning-point count.
lessons.feedback: Compare the largest-magnitude term for positive and negative inputs and test a polynomial with fewer turning points.
lessons.checkpoint: Two end-behavior items, one polynomial classification, and one turning-point bound.

lessons.title: Zeros, multiplicity, and graph shape
lessons.objective: Read zeros and multiplicities from factored form and explain crossing or touching behavior.
lessons.coverage: Factors and zeros, odd/even multiplicity, y-intercept, sign between roots, and constructing a polynomial from roots plus a scale condition.
lessons.activity: Change one root's multiplicity and predict whether the graph crosses or touches before revealing it; use a sign table as the nonvisual equivalent.
families: Annotate zeros, multiplicities, and signs for a factored polynomial
Construct a polynomial from specified roots and a point
lessons.generatorRules: Choose distinct base roots, assign multiplicities explicitly, and keep the scale point away from every root. Count multiplicity separately from distinct roots.
lessons.commonError: Equating the number of distinct roots with degree or assuming every x-intercept is a crossing.
lessons.feedback: Track the sign of the repeated factor on either side of the root.
lessons.checkpoint: Zeros, multiplicity behavior, an interval sign, and reconstruction from roots and a point.

lessons.title: Division, remainders, and factors
lessons.objective: Divide a polynomial, state quotient and remainder, and use the remainder to test a proposed factor.
lessons.coverage: Long division, synthetic division for a linear monic divisor, missing coefficients, the remainder theorem, and reconstructing dividend = divisor*quotient + remainder.
lessons.activity: Complete a division table with missing coefficients and inspect the reconstruction identity after each completed row.
families: Generate a dividend from a known divisor, quotient, and lower-degree remainder
Use evaluation to accept or reject a linear factor
lessons.generatorRules: Require remainder degree below divisor degree; include zero coefficients and nonzero remainders. State when synthetic division is applicable.
lessons.commonError: Dropping a missing-power coefficient, using the wrong sign in synthetic division, or losing the remainder.
lessons.feedback: Expand the reconstruction and highlight the first coefficient that fails to match.
lessons.checkpoint: Long division, synthetic division, factor test, and reconstruction check.

lessons.title: Finding and checking all polynomial roots
lessons.objective: Use rational-root candidates and factor reduction to obtain a complete root list, including multiplicities and complex pairs when requested.
lessons.coverage: Candidate roots versus confirmed roots, factor theorem, real-coefficient conjugate pairs, complex root counts with multiplicity, and limits of a plotted graph.
lessons.activity: Choose candidate roots, test them exactly, reduce the remaining polynomial, and compare the full root list with visible real intercepts.
families: Factor a constructed cubic or quartic using rational candidates
Audit a root list for missing multiplicities or conjugate partners
lessons.generatorRules: Build polynomials from known linear and irreducible quadratic factors. Keep arithmetic suitable for hand work; do not imply all polynomials have rational roots.
lessons.commonError: Treating every rational-root candidate as a root or assuming a graph reveals nonreal roots.
lessons.feedback: Evaluate each candidate and compare total multiplicity with degree; return to m01-l03 for a remaining quadratic.
lessons.checkpoint: Candidate generation, factor reduction, a complete complex-root list, and graph-versus-algebra interpretation.

anchor.answer: p(x)=x^3-3*x+2. Its zeros are -2 with multiplicity 1 and 1 with multiplicity 2; it crosses at -2 and touches at 1. The y-intercept is 2; left end down, right end up.

moduleExit: Explain a new polynomial using both factor structure and graph behavior; numerical plotting alone cannot satisfy the algebra objectives.
